rationale: Closes the last discriminator the NoSnapshot question carries, by source rather than by a run, so that this question ends with no dangling open item. The handler-side branch - a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot unwinding inside message handling - is reachable only if a peer can produce that message for a NoSnapshot receiver, and it cannot: a cluster's nodes share the entry type T (each node's SequencePaxos is generic over the same T and they exchange messages of that type), the sender of a Compaction::Snapshot is the node that itself called snapshot with local_only = false, and that call panics on a NoSnapshot instance before the forwarding loop runs, so a NoSnapshot node can never be sent a Snapshot compaction from a peer of its own cluster. The reachable failure mode of this question therefore stays the caller-initiated public call, which two receipts witness on a drifted and on a healthy instance. The account is rewritten as a successor with that reasoning added, the limitations updated to say what would be needed to reach the handler-side branch (a sender outside the cluster's shared entry type, which no legal configuration provides), and the same conclusion and defect claim kept; nothing was executed and no other record changed.

interpretations.rationale: The public snapshot() path reaches a panicking constructor on the crate's own placeholder snapshot type, and it does so on any instance of that type, not only on a drifted one. SequencePaxos::snapshot forwards the caller's index to InternalStorage::try_snapshot, which resolves the bound through the decided index and then, whenever that bound exceeds the current compacted index, calls create_snapshot and hence T::Snapshot::create; nothing on the path consults T::Snapshot::use_snapshots(), and for T::Snapshot = NoSnapshot that body is panic!("NoSnapshot should not be created"). The documentation for snapshot() bounds the index only by the decided index, and the Entry trait lets a configuration name NoSnapshot as its placeholder for not using snapshots, so no caller-side marker distinguishes the call as invalid. Witness on a healthy cluster: all three nodes reported accepted 6 / decided 6 with is_reconfigured true and a readable six-element decided log (receipt 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 238-240), and snapshot(Some(6), true) on the leader panicked with panicked true, the compacted index still 0 and accepted and decided still 6 (event 241), the process naming omnipaxos/src/storage/mod.rs:205 and NoSnapshot should not be created; the three nodes were still consistent afterwards (events 242-244). Witness on a drifted instance: the same call with the drifted decided bound on a leader reporting accepted 9 / decided 9 panicked in the same way (receipt 2cb2a3f1e43b4942b5bb3f42bad11091 event 129). Because both witnesses raise the panic before any storage write, the failure mode is an aborted caller with no state change and no error return. The second branch this question named, a panic raised inside message handling by a forwarded compaction, is closed by source: SequencePaxos::snapshot forwards a Compaction::Snapshot to the peers only when the call itself succeeded (local_only = false and result.is_ok()), the peers' handle_compaction then calls the same snapshot entry, so a NoSnapshot receiver would indeed unwind inside its message handler - but such a message cannot arise inside a cluster, because every node of one cluster instantiates SequencePaxos over the same entry type T, the sender is by construction the node whose own snapshot call runs first, and on a NoSnapshot instance that call panics before the forwarding loop. Reaching the handler-side abort would therefore need a sender outside the cluster's shared entry type, which no legal configuration of this library provides and this harness cannot construct; what remains reachable is the caller-initiated call witnessed above.
counterevidence: The crate documents NoSnapshot as a placeholder for configurations that do not use snapshots and implements create and merge as panicking stubs, so the panic is that type's declared behaviour when invoked; the deviation is that the documented public path invokes it instead of refusing or erroring, and the caller receives no CompactionErr.

The call is a user-initiated snapshot request, so a caller that knows its entry type cannot use snapshots could avoid it; the defect is the abort rather than a silent wrong result, and no data is lost because the unwind happens before the storage write (compacted index 0 and unchanged indices in both witnesses).
The drift is not required: the healthy control shows the same panic with a consistent six-entry decided log, so this account does not depend on the parent investigation's index accounting.

The handler-side branch is not merely untested but unreachable inside a cluster of one entry type, because the forwarding node is the node that would panic first; this narrows the blast radius to callers that invoke snapshot() themselves on a non-snapshot configuration.
limitations: Only one entry type was used for the witnesses (the harness's Value with Snapshot = NoSnapshot); whether a derive-macro-generated Snapshot type defaults to NoSnapshot and therefore inherits the panic was not established.

The handler-side branch was not exercised and cannot be produced inside one cluster, since all nodes share the entry type; the reasoning that a NoSnapshot node is never sent a Snapshot compaction rests on the source order (the sender's own snapshot call panics before it forwards) rather than on an observed message.
The panic is observed through catch_unwind, which reports the abort of the call but not the state a process without the guard would be in; no restart or supervision behaviour was exercised.

Whether the crate considers snapshot() valid for non-snapshot configurations is not settled by documentation: the snapshot() doc comment bounds the index by the decided index and does not mention use_snapshots(), which is the basis for treating the abort as a defect rather than a caller error.

No execution compared a NoSnapshot instance that has already compacted by other means (a forwarded trim, for instance) with a fresh one; both witnesses had a compacted index of 0 when the call panicked.
